noeuds.schema: Inputs: Object, Columns, Rows, Model objects (names separated by commas)
noeuds.role: Splits object A (the board) into columns and rows and puts in each cell a copy of a model object picked at random (at least 3 models, names separated by commas). There is never a match at the start, and the pieces drop in from the top. Use it before “Play on the grid (match 3)”.
noeuds.exemple: at the start, an 8 x 8 grid of candies "red, orange, yellow, green, blue, pink".

noeuds.schema: Inputs: Object, Finger X position, Finger Y position  →  Outputs: For each matched piece / Move finished / Swap refused
noeuds.role: The heart of a match-3 game (Candy Crush style), to put under “Finger held down”. Touching a piece selects it, touching its neighbour (or sliding the finger to it) swaps them. The swap only stays if it lines up 3 or more identical pieces; otherwise they go back (“Swap refused”). Each matched piece starts “For each matched piece” (the involved object is the piece), then disappears; pieces fall, new ones arrive and combos happen by themselves. When everything is still: “Move finished”. With no possible move, the grid shuffles itself.
noeuds.exemple: “For each matched piece”: +10 points and sparkles on the piece; “Move finished”: one move less.

noeuds.role: Moves all the pieces of object A's grid to new places, without creating a match and keeping at least one possible move.
noeuds.exemple: a "Shuffle" button when the player is stuck.

noeuds.role: Randomly swaps the places of all objects with the chosen tag (Object A = "# tag"). Their child objects follow them.
noeuds.exemple: shuffle the cards of a memory game at the start, or the cups of a shell game.
